newsitem.title: UK: UK retail sales up 0.6 pct in June.
newsitem.headline: UK retail sales up 0.6 pct in June.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) released the following seasonally adjusted data on UK retail sales in June.
RETAIL SALES VOLUME June May (May prev)
The Reuters consensus forecast was for a rise of 0.4 percent in the month and 4.5 percent year-on-year.
BY SECTOR (percentage gain, minus indicates fall)
The average weekly non-seasonally adjusted value of retail sales in June was 3.32 billion stg, 5.8 percent up on June 1996.
In value terms, retail sales rose by 5.9 percent in the three months to the end of June on the same period a year earlier.
* Highest three-month on three-month a year ago rate since December 1988 when it was 5.5 percent.
** The ONS said the three-month/three-month increase in household goods sales was the highest since at least 1986, when records began.
The June trading period was a five-week one running from June 1 to July 5.
The ONS said there was not a lot of detailed evidence on spending of windfall payments. But it said windfall cash would expected to be spent largely on household goods, where sales rose dramatically.
It said spending on household goods was 150 million stg higher than it had expected last month, adding that most of that could be attributed to windfall cash, although there was no hard evidence.
The ONS also said bad weather in June would have had some negative effect on sales generally.
